question: Atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) is the most common congenital heart defect in Down syndrome, and duodenal atresia presenting with a 'double-bubble' sign on X-ray is a characteristic gastrointestinal association.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. AVSD is the most common CHD in Down syndrome (not VSD or ASD alone), and duodenal atresia is the hallmark GI anomaly. Both are high-yield associations that guide the systematic neonatal evaluation of every child with trisomy 21.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. AVSD (endocardial cushion defect) is the hallmark cardiac lesion in Down syndrome, occurring in ~40–50% of those with CHD; early surgical repair is essential before pulmonary hypertension develops. Duodenal atresia — associated in ~30% of cases with Down syndrome — gives the classic double-bubble sign (dilated stomach + first part of duodenum) on plain X-ray.
